name: Ahaziah
overview: Ahaziah was a male king of Israel and the son of Ahab, as recorded in 1 Kings 22:40. His reign is noted in Scripture primarily through his royal status and lineage, with no specific tribal affiliation or additional personal notes provided.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahaziah means 'YHWH has upheld,' reflecting a theophoric element common in Hebrew names, although it was not given by God. He is also referred to by the titles 'King of Samaria' and 'King of Israel,' indicating his rule over the northern kingdom, as seen in 2 Kings 1:3 and 2 Chronicles 20:35.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Ahaziah as the son of Ahab, establishing his royal lineage in the northern kingdom of Israel. Beyond this father-son relationship, no other family connections are detailed in the provided facts.
scriptureSignificance: Ahaziah's significance lies in his position as a successor to Ahab and his role in the continuation of Ahab's dynasty, which was marked by unfaithfulness to God. His brief reign illustrates the consequences of following in the sinful ways of his father and associates, highlighting the rapid spiritual decline that can occur under ungodly influence. His story serves as a cautionary example within the biblical narrative about the dangers of departing from God's commands.
